sections.h2: Where Sarasota County keeps its property records
sections.html:
The Clerk of the Circuit Court, whose title also includes Comptroller, holds the Official Records, which is the public file for land paper in the county. Anyone can search the index online, and the title agent on your sale will search it as well.

The online search screen opens to a public access group with no login. Search by last or business name, first name, instrument number, a filing date range, or book and page. The index starts on January 1, 1990, so very old papers need a different route.

A separate tab covers marriage records, plats and condominiums, and property fraud alerts. Certified copies go through their own login, and expect a wait of up to 24 business hours.

sections.h2: Document types a seller should look for
sections.html:
The document type menu runs well past a hundred entries. The ones that matter to a seller are DEED, MORTGAGE, SATISFACTION OF MORTGAGE, CLAIM OF LIEN/LIEN, LIS PENDENS, JUDGMENT, TAX LIEN/MISC and the tax deed entries.

Search your own name before you accept an offer, and watch for these:

  • A mortgage with no satisfaction after it, which means the loan still sits on the house.
  • A claim of lien or notice to owner from a contractor, often the result of unpaid repair work.
  • A lis pendens, a sign of a pending lawsuit that touches the property.
  • A judgment or tax lien under your name that could attach to the house.
  • An easement or restriction a buyer will ask about.

The list also includes probate entries such as letters of administration and personal representative oaths, so an inherited house usually leaves a visible paper trail.

A search shows the top 500 records only, so narrow a common surname with a first name or a date range. Every hit carries an instrument number you can use to pull the same paper again later.

Labels follow the clerk's own list, and some are easy to miss when a house has a long history:

  • AGREEMENT FOR DEED, the label for a contract for deed.
  • NOTICE OF HOMESTEAD and DECLARATION OF DOMICILE, which relate to residence claims.
  • WARRANT DELINQUENT TAX and FEDERAL TAX LIEN, which sit against an owner and can shadow a closing.
  • DECLARATION OF CONDO and plat entries, handled on the Plats and Condos tab.
  • MOBILE HOME TITLE RETIREMENT, which matters if a manufactured home became real property.

PROBATE, FAMILY and CONFIDENTIAL are separate type codes, so a case file can show up beside the land records.

The first page of a document costs $10.00 and every page after it costs $8.50, for paper up to 8.5 by 14 inches. Plats are priced separately at $30.00 and $15.00.

A document with more than four names pays $1.00 for each name beyond four. State law stacks a base page fee, a records modernization charge and a technology charge, which is how the clerk arrives at those totals.

A notice of commencement or declaration of domicile adds a $3.50 attestation fee. Call the recording desk for a total before mailing anything.

The clerk charges 70 cents for every $100 of consideration, the same statewide rate, with no local variation in Sarasota County.

Round the price up to the next $100 first, and the minimum is $0.70. A deed is taxable even if it is never recorded. Each party is liable no matter what the contract assigns, so the state can pursue either side.

The buyer's loan brings its own charges: $0.35 per $100 of the obligation as mortgage stamps, plus $0.20 per $100 as intangible tax, figured on the exact amount with no rounding. These attach to the mortgage, which is recorded after your deed.

Some transfers escape the tax. A probate personal representative's deed is listed as not taxable, and a divorce deed for the marital home is exempt. The clerk wants any exemption visible on the face of the document, so have the closing agent check the wording first.

sections.h2: Extra clerk fees for liens and notices
sections.html:
Some filings trigger extra clerk work. A notice of contest of lien, notice of homestead or notice of interest carries a $7.00 certificate of service, plus certified mail at the current postal rate.

Moving a construction lien to a bond costs $20.00 for the first lien and $10.00 for each additional one, with an $8.50 charge to approve the surety bond. For a broker lien the clerk lists $15.00 first and $7.50 each added.

If you learn of a contractor lien before closing, budget for these fees. Clearing the lien is usually a condition of the buyer's title policy.

Sign up for Property Fraud Alerts, a free service from the clerk. Whenever a deed, mortgage or similar paper is recorded in the county under a name you registered, you get an email.

The search screen has a Property Fraud Alerts tab, and the property appraiser urges owners to register. Enter the owner's name and any business name that holds title, ideally before the house sits empty or changes hands.

If an alert arrives for a filing you never signed, call the clerk and an attorney, and keep the instrument number. If an LLC holds title, register the company name too.

sections.h2: How records connect to the tax bill
sections.html:
Recording the deed is what updates ownership for the tax offices. A deed recorded late can leave the new owner without a bill on time.

Proration is settled on the closing statement. You credit the buyer for the months you owned the house, and the collector takes no partial payment from you. Our Sarasota County property tax guide covers the calendar and discounts.

A sale also ends a long-held Save Our Homes cap, because a change of ownership returns the parcel to just value the next January 1. Transfers between spouses are among the exceptions.

Print your own recording history and keep it beside the contract. A short checklist:

  • Look for open mortgages, liens and judgments tied to your name.
  • Make sure every owner named on the deed can sign.
  • Ask the closing agent whether any stamp exemption applies.
  • Sign in front of two witnesses, as Florida requires when conveying land.
  • Register for fraud alerts before the house sits empty.

For an inherited house, the clerk's file shows whether letters of administration were issued. Summary administration is allowed when the non-exempt estate is $150,000 or less, or the owner died over two years ago.

A sale goes smoothest when you do the paper work first. Search your name and the property, list every open item, and work with the title company to clear each one before a buyer's deadline arrives. Ask for written payoff letters for every mortgage or lien, and keep the recorded satisfaction numbers once they post.

After closing, the deed is recorded and the stamps are paid from your proceeds or the buyer's funds, as the contract provides. Search the index again a few weeks later and confirm that the deed to the buyer and the satisfaction of your loan both appear. Save a copy of each for your files.

A cash buyer still needs a clean record, and a cash sale skips only the lender's steps.

faqs.q: Is the Sarasota County records search free?
faqs.a: Yes. The public search needs no login and accepts a name, instrument number or date range. Its index starts January 1, 1990.

faqs.q: What does a Sarasota County deed filing cost?
faqs.a: Expect $10.00 for page one and $8.50 for each later page, with indexing free through four names. Deed stamp tax is billed on top.

faqs.q: Who pays the stamps on a Sarasota sale?
faqs.a: Every party is liable under state law. The purchase contract assigns the cost, and the closing agent usually collects it.

faqs.q: Can I get a certified copy?
faqs.a: Yes, for $2.00 a document through the certified copy login. Allow up to 24 business hours.

faqs.q: Does a cash sale change the recording steps?
faqs.a: No. The deed is still recorded and the stamps still apply, and liens still get cleared first.
